thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (hosted-us-east-1). p95 -> 240ms, p99 -> 1.8s, elevated error rate 1.6% (stream stalls).

oncall-jen: paging. I'm on it. grabbing logs and looking at the routing dashboard.

sre-ryan: seeing tail stalls correlated with specific GPU hostpool: gpu-pool-e-3a. KV cache misses and multiple retransmits.

ml-ava: model telemetry shows increase in attention recompute on longer sequences; but this looks like infra-level stalls rather than model hang.

infra-marcus: hardware telemetry: node gpu-03 reports repeated correctable ECC events and fan speed ramping -> thermal throttle entries. Temp moved 83C -> 92C then throttle.

oncall-jen: ok, mark impacted customer tier: several PLG customers hit intermittent streaming stalls, 2 customers reported client timeouts. tagging @customer-success-lina.

customer-success-lina: notifying the two affected accounts on their support threads. no escalations yet but they're seeing 503/timeout clients.

sre-ryan: immediate mitigation: taking gpu-03 out of rotation, re-route new streams away. plan: drain in-flight KV cache and let existing sessions finish small window, then cordon/drain.

infra-marcus: running: `kubectl annotate node gpu-03 maintenance=true && ./drain-node.sh gpu-03 --grace 30s`

ml-ava: can we fallback to a CPU-safe model variant for long streaming sessions on that hostpool while we remediate? config snippet below:
```json
{"route_policy":"fallback","target":"cpu-small-quant","threshold_ms":800}
```

oncall-jen: rolling fallback applied to hostpool-level routing for 4m. observing new requests routed to cpu-small-quant in us-east-1-b.

incident-bot: NOTE: Rollout ID r-2026-04-05-11 applied, traffic shift 18% -> fallback variant. Metrics will update in ~60s.

sre-ryan: draining complete, cordoned. moving gpu-03 to maintenance. Running hardware checks: vendor diag collecting ECC hist, power rails stable, but fan control logs show repeated oscillation.

infra-marcus: I recommended thermal firmware update and forced fan profile to high. filing ticket with vendor: HWS-12190.

pm-olivia: customers want ETA. what's impact window?

oncall-jen: right now mitigations reduced p99 from 1.8s -> 320ms for new requests. historical sessions that hit stalls may still see tail gaps for up to ~45s while KV accepts remaining tokens. overall error rate dropping to 0.2%. ETA for full recovery: 40-60m including hardware runbook and vendor confirmation.

customer-success-lina: sent interim notice to customers with current mitigations and ETA. they asked if we will proactively move any scheduled jobs off this pool.

ml-ava: recommend longer-term: increase prefix caching on streaming for this model and add model-quantized fallback for this hostpool. Also add a health-check that flags repeated ECC_correctable > 5 per hour for auto-drain.

sre-ryan: agree. I'll add an alert rule: `alert: GPUCorrectableECCSpike` threshold 5 in 1h -> auto-drain trigger.

infra-marcus: vendor advised swapping the GPU module if ECC continues after firmware bump. backup nodes available in pool; capacity is OK.

oncall-jen: documenting postmortem notes in incident tracker. assigning follow-ups: hardware ticket -> infra-marcus, routing fallback improvement -> ml-ava, alert rule -> sre-ryan, customer comms -> customer-success-lina.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated; severity -> SEV2; next update in 30m or on significant change.

pm-olivia: thanks all. please drop any postmortem links and SLA hit calc in this thread.

sre-ryan: initial SLA calc: brief p99 breach for ~18 minutes, estimated customer-visible request failures ~0.03% of daily traffic. will produce exact numbers in postmortem.

oncall-jen: closing live coordination. leaving thread open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
